items.title: Street door and buzzer
items.body: The street door code is 1948#. Then buzz 4B — I'll hear it if I'm home. After 4pm on weekdays, and all weekend, the desk is empty, so use the code and come straight up. Please don't prop the street door.

items.title: Spare key in the lockbox
items.body: Black lockbox on the stairwell railing, just past 4B. Code 4421. The spare is the brass key. Lock it back in before you leave, even if you're only out for a minute with the dog. The doorman knows the box is ours.

images.caption: Black lockbox on the stairwell railing, just past 4B.

items.title: What to tell the doorman
items.body: Luis covers weekdays until 4. Andre covers Saturday morning. Say you are here for Alex Chen in 4B — a first name alone isn't enough and they will not send you up. If the desk is empty, the door code still works.

items.title: Wi-Fi
items.body: Network: ChenNest. Password: marigold-22, all lower case. If a video call stutters, ChenGuest / guest22 is the older router and it's fine for maps and music.

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.body:
Alex, 917-555-0188. The super is Mr. Ruiz in the basement, 212-555-0160. Building emergency line 212-555-0100. Nearest ER is Lenox Health Greenwich Village, about a ten-minute walk west.

Miso's vet is Village Vet on Hudson, 212-555-0194. The carrier is on top of the hall closet.

items.title: Leave these alone
items.body:
The oak desk in the living room, the vinyl crates beside it, and the framed print over the piano. Please don't straighten that print — it was hung off on purpose.

Street-facing blinds stay half down when you leave. The bedroom blackout stays up.

items.title: Quiet hours for 4A
items.body: The neighbor in 4A works nights and sleeps through the morning. No vacuum before 10am or after 7pm. The dishwasher is fine anytime. If Miso barks at the door, a hand on her chest usually ends it.

items.title: Shoes off
items.body: Shoes come off on the tray inside the door. The floors were refinished in March and a heel mark shows. Slippers are in the basket if you want them.

items.title: Miso — harness, not the collar
items.body:
Miso is a four-year-old shiba. She is polite with people and opinionated about pigeons. The blue harness hangs on the hook by the door — use that, not the collar. The collar is only there so she has a tag. She pulls toward the river. A thirty-minute loop that includes the pier is the good walk.

She slipped a collar on 10th Avenue last year. That is why the harness is the rule, for Jordan and for whoever walks her next.

images.caption: Blue harness on the hook by the door. Use this, not the collar.

items.title: Feeding — one cup, and only after 5
items.body:
One cup of the salmon kibble, from the glass jar on the lower open shelf, with a splash of warm water. Only on walks that end after 5pm. Morning and midday walkers leave the bowl alone.

The tin on the counter is guest treats and they upset her stomach. This note started after a walk with Sam, when a second cup made her sick. It applies to every walker, not just Sam.

items.title: Evening pill
items.body: Apoquel is in the cabinet above the sink, left of the mugs. Half a tablet in a piece of cheese, on the evening walk only. The morning walker skips it. If she spits it out, leave the half on the saucer and text Alex.

items.title: How to run the laundry
items.body: Towels on hot. Everything else cold. Detergent is the unscented jug under the kitchen sink — one short pour, not a full cap. Skip the dryer sheets; the box under the sink is for guests who ask. The linen shirt gets a hanger, not the tumble dryer.

items.title: Hamper and folding
items.body: The hamper is in the bedroom closet, left side. Fold on the bed in three stacks: lights, darks, towels. Alex puts them away. Please don't put clean clothes back in the hamper to be helpful.

items.title: Kitchen and the espresso machine
items.body:
Load the dishwasher. Don't start it if it's less than half full. Wipe the espresso machine with a dry cloth only — the steam wand spots if it's wet.

Compost under the sink goes out when it's past half. The chute is at the end of the hall, not the trash room.

images.caption: Wipe the espresso machine with a dry cloth only.

items.title: Plants
items.body: The fiddle leaf by the south window gets one cup only if the soil is dry an inch down. The succulents on the sill are on their own, even if they look dramatic. Please don't mist anything near the piano.

images.caption: One cup for the fiddle leaf, and only if the soil is dry an inch down.

items.title: Where the vacuum lives
items.body: Hall closet, bottom, behind the winter boots. The wand clips to the inside of the door. Empty the cup into the chute if it's past the line — not into the kitchen trash. No vacuum before 10am; 4A is asleep.

images.caption: This is where the vacuum lives.

items.title: Cleaning caddy and towels
items.body:
The caddy is under the bathroom sink. The clear bottle is a vinegar mix for the floors. The blue bottle is glass only. The green soap is for hands; the white pump is face wash, please leave it.

Extra hand towels are in the linen closet, second shelf. Swap the hand towel if it's damp.

items.title: Trash and recycling
items.body: Kitchen trash goes down the chute by the elevator. Recycling is the blue bin in the basement. The basement door uses the same code as the street door. Break boxes down. Bottles go in with the caps off — fussy, and it's what the building asked for.

items.title: The piano
items.body: It's a Yamaha U1. The bench height is set; please leave the felt alone. Sheet music for the week stays on the stand. The metronome is inside the bench. A glass of water is fine. No mugs on the lid, ever.

images.caption: Yamaha U1. No mugs on the lid.

items.title: What we're working on
items.body:
Bach Invention in F, then the first Chopin nocturne if the hand is loose. Please don't assign new scales until the F major is clean. Recording on your phone is welcome.

Alex practices after 8pm, so the bench may have moved. Slide it back to the dent in the rug.
